Common initial k-point configuration, oblivious sequence and uniform positive rational distances remain explicit.

prior_work_distinction: A1 summarizes an unverified arbitrary-metric result. This proves a uniform-metric subclass with a fully bounded per-request fair-bit implementation and horizon-free error control, adding meaningful implementation scope beyond stating classical marking.
scope_assessment: For every finite uniform rational metric of distance Δ>0 and 2≤k<n, a single randomized bit algorithm uses polynomial preprocessing and worst-case polynomial work per request in L+log(t+1), and has expected cost≤2Hk·OPT+2kΔ for every finite oblivious sequence from a common initial k-point configuration. This satisfies the prompt on uniform metrics, not arbitrary finite metrics.
